title: The average is twenty-one minutes and one ticket in ten waits nine hours
variant: A distribution, because the mean describes nobody in it
prompt: Quarterly numbers for the support desk. Response times look fine on paper and people keep complaining.
note: The leanest of the three and the one about measurement rather than subject: every finding is a statement about how the numbers are being reported. Median and 90th percentile sit in adjacent tiles because reporting both is the recommendation; the distribution shows that 61% of tickets are in the first bar and the mean falls in a bucket almost nobody is in; and the by-hour chart is deliberately linear rather than log, so the working day comes out as a row of slivers -- which is the finding, not a rendering problem. The out-of-hours tail turns out to be a rota question, which is the kind of thing an average can hide indefinitely.
